summary: A 1880 iron tower and wood-frame keeper house at Harding Beach on Stage Harbor; automated in 1933, sold, and privately owned since.

lens.where: Archive gives fourth order; LighthouseFriends gives fifth order (see notes)

structures.note: 36 ft from base to lantern centre per the Archive; LighthouseFriends gives 48 ft (see notes).

access.note: Privately owned; grounds, dwelling and tower closed. Visible from a distance across Stage Harbor.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources differ on whether the light is still lit. The Archive says it is no longer an active aid to navigation; LighthouseFriends says a nearby skeleton tower is the active aid. The record's active status appears to describe that nearby tower, not this one.

notes_for_editor: (1) Tower and lens conflict: LighthouseFriends gives a 48 ft iron tower and a fifth-order lens; the Archive gives 36 ft from base to lantern centre and a fourth-order lens (Original Optic). The record's 11 m matches the Archive. Both are stated in the story. (2) Mills Gunderson: LighthouseFriends records his death on 15 June 1918 and says he 'hung himself in a shed for unknown reasons'; the story gives the date and says the reasons are not recorded, without describing the manner further. The Archive roster dates Stanley Gunderson's keeping from 1919 and LighthouseFriends says he replaced his father after June 1918. Unresolved; the story notes the roster date. (3) The Trilby tow: the 1915 Bulletin gives '12 September' with no year. The FY1915 Commissioner list covers 1914-15 and names Howard without naming the tow, so 1914 is an assumption; the story gives the day and month only. LighthouseFriends dates the horse letter 19 December 1914; the Bulletin's December 18 text is OCR-damaged. (4) Nearly all of the keepers' narrative (appointments and salaries, the 1913, 1914 and 1929 rescues, the 1920-33 commendations and Prohibition anecdote, the 1933 automation and protest, the sale, the later posts) comes from LighthouseFriends alone, which cites a 1950 Coast Guard historical paper (Eldridge) it does not reproduce. Not read. (5) The 1878 Board recommendation and the 1879 appropriation come from LighthouseFriends; the Board's 1878 report is not in the corpus (the Board volumes there start in 1891). (6) The 1935 buyer and the family that has owned the property since early 1936 are named by LighthouseFriends. They are private residents and are not named in the story. (7) The Life-Saving Service narratives for Stage Harbor entrance (1884 to 1907) describe wrecks and assists at the harbor mouth, not at the light; not tied to the station, so not used. Stage Harbor, Maine entries are a different place. (8) The record's 'Fl W 6s' characteristic, 8.5 m focal height and 7 nm range are not verified here and are not used. The record's 'Stage Harbor' status conflicts are discussed in resolved_conflicts. (9) Two newspaper searches (1929-1935) found only unrelated pages. (10) No photos added. No corrections proposed: the record's tower height matches the Archive and the difference with LighthouseFriends is recorded here.
